deck.title: Directory Services
deck.analogy: On-prem AD is the head office's filing room: Managed AD is a full branch filing room, AD Connector is a phone line to head office, Simple AD is a budget photocopy.

subtopics.title: The three options (the table to memorize)

cards.front: What is Active Directory (AD) and what does it store?

back.answer: Microsoft's on-prem directory: the corporate phonebook plus master keyring, storing users, computers and groups, and authenticating logins.
back.explanation: Users log into a domain like corp.example.com. LDAP is the protocol to talk to it; domain join enrolls a machine into it.

cards.front: Which Windows services in AWS need a directory to authenticate against (Directory Services context)?

back.answer: FSx for Windows File Server, Amazon WorkSpaces, and RDS for SQL Server.
back.explanation: The exam question is which of the three directory options fits, not whether you need one.

cards.front: What are the three AWS Directory Service options and their analogy?

back.answer: Managed Microsoft AD = full branch filing room; AD Connector = phone line to head office; Simple AD = budget photocopy.
back.mnemonic: Full copy w/ trust / phone line / budget clone.

cards.front: What is each directory option really: AWS Managed Microsoft AD vs AD Connector vs Simple AD?

back.answer: Managed Microsoft AD is real Microsoft AD in AWS; AD Connector is a proxy forwarding auth; Simple AD is a Samba-based AD-compatible clone.

cards.sourceHeading: The three options (the table to memorize)

cards.front: Which directory options store users in AWS: Managed Microsoft AD, AD Connector, Simple AD?

back.answer: Managed Microsoft AD and Simple AD store users in AWS; AD Connector stores nothing in AWS.

cards.sourceHeading: The three options (the table to memorize)

cards.front: How does each directory option work with on-prem AD?

back.answer: Managed AD: two-way trust. AD Connector: only redirects to on-prem. Simple AD: no trust, standalone only.
back.explanation: A trust means two forests honor each other's logins, so users from either side can access either side without syncing passwords.

cards.sourceHeading: The three options (the table to memorize)

cards.front: MFA support across Managed Microsoft AD, AD Connector and Simple AD?

back.answer: Managed AD: yes. AD Connector: yes, via on-prem RADIUS. Simple AD: no MFA.

cards.sourceHeading: The three options (the table to memorize)

cards.front: Best-fit use for each: Managed Microsoft AD, AD Connector, Simple AD?

back.answer: Managed AD: full AD in cloud, domain join, hybrid trust. Connector: keep identities on-prem. Simple AD: cheap basic LDAP, under 5,000 users.

cards.sourceHeading: The three options (the table to memorize)

cards.front: Simple AD is suited to organizations up to roughly what user count?

back.answer: Fewer than 5,000 users.

cards.sourceHeading: The three options (the table to memorize)

cards.front: When is AWS Managed Microsoft AD the answer?

back.answer: When you need real AD machinery in AWS: EC2 Windows domain join, MFA, RDS SQL Server/FSx/WorkSpaces integration, or trust with on-prem.
back.explanation: Spot phrases: "full AD features in the cloud" or "trust with on-prem".

cards.front: When is AD Connector the answer, and what is its corollary risk?

back.answer: When identities must never be stored in the cloud; every auth redirects to on-prem. If the VPN/Direct Connect link dies, authentication dies.
back.explanation: It's a pipe, not a directory.

cards.front: When is Simple AD the answer?

back.answer: When the scenario says lowest cost, basic LDAP, small organization, and nothing mentions trust, MFA, or on-prem integration.

cards.front: Trap: "Connect Simple AD to on-prem AD with a trust" — possible?

back.answer: No. Simple AD supports no trust and no MFA; either word eliminates it.

cards.examTip: trust or MFA = not Simple AD

cards.front: Trap: Can AD Connector be used as a standalone directory?

back.answer: No. AD Connector requires an existing on-prem AD to proxy to.
back.explanation: A phone line with no head office connects to nothing.
back.mnemonic: Phone line needs a head office.

cards.front: Which services require a directory, and what is the real exam question?

back.answer: FSx for Windows, WorkSpaces, RDS for SQL Server (Windows Auth) all require one; the question is which of the three options fits.

cards.front: FSx for Windows: existing on-prem identities vs need MFA and cloud-resident AD — which directory?

back.answer: On-prem identities: Managed AD with trust, or AD Connector. MFA plus cloud-resident AD: Managed Microsoft AD.

cards.front: Deploy FSx for Windows File Server; users must authenticate with existing on-prem AD identities. Which directory?

back.answer: Managed Microsoft AD with a trust, or AD Connector.

choices.text: Managed Microsoft AD with trust, or AD Connector

choices.why: Not a Windows directory for FSx.

cards.front: Security policy requires no user identities stored in the cloud. Which Directory Service option?

back.answer: AD Connector.
back.explanation: Proxy only; all auth redirected on-prem.

choices.why: Still a directory in the cloud.

cards.front: Small company needs a low-cost, basic LDAP-compatible directory for one application. Which option?

back.answer: Simple AD.
back.explanation: Cheap Samba standalone, fine under ~5,000 users.

choices.why: Low-cost basic LDAP for small orgs.

cards.front: EC2 Windows instances must join a domain, and MFA is required. Which option?

back.answer: AWS Managed Microsoft AD.
back.explanation: Real AD: domain join plus MFA; Simple AD has neither MFA nor trust.

cards.front: Establish a two-way trust between AWS and the on-prem domain so users on both sides access resources. Which option?

back.answer: AWS Managed Microsoft AD.
back.explanation: The only option supporting trust relationships.

cards.front: RDS for SQL Server with Windows Authentication for corporate users. Which directory?

back.answer: AWS Managed Microsoft AD (add a trust for on-prem users).

choices.why: Direct RDS integration; trust for on-prem.
Needs on-prem AD, no direct RDS fit.

cards.front: WorkSpaces desktops must authenticate against on-prem AD without replicating the directory. Which option?

back.answer: AD Connector.
back.explanation: Phone line: auth flows back on-prem.

choices.why: Proxies auth to on-prem, no replication.

cards.front: Keyword: **"Full AD features in AWS"**

back.answer: Managed Microsoft AD

cards.front: Keyword: **"Trust relationship with on-prem"**

back.answer: Managed Microsoft AD (two-way trust)

cards.front: Keyword: **"MFA + domain join"**

back.answer: Managed Microsoft AD

cards.front: Keyword: **"No identities stored in cloud"**

back.answer: AD Connector

cards.front: Keyword: **"Proxy / redirect auth to on-prem"**

back.answer: AD Connector

cards.front: Keyword: **"Low cost, basic LDAP, small org"**

back.answer: Simple AD

cards.front: Keyword: **"No trust, no MFA"**

back.answer: Simple AD's limits

cards.front: Keyword: **"FSx Windows / WorkSpaces / RDS SQL Server"**

back.answer: All need a directory — pick from the three

back.answer: Full copy w/ trust / phone line / budget clone
